behavior: Secretive and often concealed; forages mainly on the ground for grass seeds, taking more insects during the breeding season. Breeding males sing from exposed perches and vigorously defend territories. Migrates chiefly at night.
field_marks: Adult male has a deep blue head, bright green back, and scarlet-red underparts and rump.
Female and immature plumage is mostly bright yellow-green, with a paler eyering.
Small, stocky proportions with a short neck and rounded body.
Stubby, thick, conical seed-cracking bill, gray to dark in color.
Dark eyes and dusky gray-brown legs and feet.
Wings and tail are relatively dark, with a compact wing and medium-length tail.
habitat: Dense brush and semi-open habitats with low cover, including grassy or weedy edges, riparian thickets, scrub, hedgerows, open-woodland understory, overgrown fields, and tropical forest margins or densely vegetated savannas.
